summary: No single dataset gives size and shape for related species from fetal stages to adulthood; the pieces exist separately. Dryad holds multi-species ontogenetic morphometric series (Anolis embryonic limb bones for 15 species, 10.5061/dryad.jsxksn08d; shape coordinates for adults and ontogenetic series, 10.5061/dryad.t4b8gtj5j; macaque skull and bovid horn ontogeny), MorphoSource has 445 juvenile-tagged 3D specimens without an age field, and BIA has stage-resolved embryo microCT for mouse and human only.
next_step: Download the two Dryad series (5 MB each, CC0) to confirm taxa and stage coverage, then pre-register a disparity-vs-stage test on Anolis limbs (embryonic) and on the multi-species shape-coordinate series; the mammalian fetal-to-adult contrast would need to be compiled from literature.
obstacles_confirmed: Fetal and juvenile series are taxonomically sparse next to adult specimens: MorphoSource juvenile hits are 445 of a much larger adult-dominated archive and carry no stage field.
Embryos of related species are unevenly sampled: stage-resolved embryo imaging in BIA is mouse and human.
e-Mouse Atlas was unreachable during this scout.
